findings.title: #842's CENTS_PARTICULARS misses four cents-typed basis keys, so money still renders as raw sen in the same disclosure
findings.evidence: periodic-adjustments-table.tsx's new `const CENTS_PARTICULARS = new Set<string>(["settled_cents"])` and its comment 'settled_cents (#797) is the only one today (see periodic-adjustment.ts's ADJUSTMENT_FIELDS comment)'. That claim is falsified by the two sources it cites. (a) The canonical basis builder, packages/db/migrations/0212_payroll_settled_cents.sql:294-330, stores `opening_cents`, `closing_cents`, `adjustment_cents` and `amount_cents` in the STOCK branch's basis and `amount_cents` + `settled_cents` in the PAYROLL branch's basis. (b) apps/web/lib/work/periodic-adjustment.ts:539-547's ADJUSTMENT_FIELDS lists five cents fields: openingCents, closingCents, adjustmentCents, amountCents, settledCents. The disclosure loops `Object.entries(row.basis)` for every purpose, so a real payroll row renders basis.amount_cents as a bare integer directly beside the column's Money-rendered amount_cents (the exact 'same figure told two different ways' the ticket names), and every stock row renders three raw minor-unit integers. The lane's own test fixture (`row({ obligation_kind, settled_cents })`) omits amount_cents from the basis, which is why no cell caught it. The ticket's Out-of-scope line ('none is cents-typed today') is the source of the error; work-order rule 6 asks for the assumption to be stated in the report when a brief turns out to be wrong - instead the false claim was committed into a source comment and the report is silent. Also violates the lane's own standing rule 'Money always renders as RM 1,060.00, never raw sen'.
findings.required_fix: Either extend CENTS_PARTICULARS to {settled_cents, amount_cents, opening_cents, closing_cents, adjustment_cents} with a cell per branch (a stock row and a payroll row whose basis carries amount_cents), or, if the wave will not widen #842, delete the false 'only one today' claim from the comment and record the residual in the report and as a follow-up ticket.

findings.title: #904's poll tick costs 5-6 reads, against use-settle-poll's own documented 'onTick: One read' contract and the FIX ROUND 1 that cut the sibling poll from four to one
findings.evidence: document-detail.tsx passes `onTick: () => void reload()`, where `reload` re-runs `loadDocumentDetail` - apps/web/lib/documents/loaders.ts:116-135 issues five parallel reads (documents, document_filings, document_extractions, journal_entries, document_processing_tasks_visible) plus a sixth (document_regions) whenever a current extraction exists. apps/web/lib/documents/use-settle-poll.ts:42 types onTick as '/** One read. Errors are the caller's to render; this hook only stops asking. */'. apps/web/README.md:495-503 records the sibling receipts poll's law in bold - 'A tick costs ONE read' - and says FIX ROUND 1 existed precisely because 'the tick re-ran the whole derivation - up to four reads a tick under the caller's own JWT, the heaviest of them a SECURITY INVOKER RPC'. #904 re-introduces a heavier version of the pattern that fix removed, on the same tab, and neither the code comment, the README nor the final report records the cost. Bounded at DEFAULT_MAX_TICKS=12, so a worst case of ~72 reads per open panel.
findings.required_fix: Either narrow onTick to a tasks-only re-read (listProcessingTasksForDocument + a setState for that slice) so the hook's one-read contract holds, or accept the whole-bundle reload explicitly: say so in document-detail.tsx's comment, amend use-settle-poll.ts's onTick doc, and record the read-cost tradeoff in the lane report and in apps/web/README.md's Documents section.

findings.title: the new poll's `exhausted` state is not surfaced, so a long-running task ends in a silent stop

With the defaults (12 ticks, 1.5s base, 15s cap) the panel stops re-reading after roughly two minutes and shows no affordance and no statement that it stopped. Not an AC - AC2 only asks that polling stop when every task is terminal, which it does.

summary: All eight tickets were really built and all their acceptance criteria are met on the evidence re-run here: 75 cells across the ten touched test files pass, pnpm lint exits 0, pnpm typecheck exits 0, check-frozen-workflows.mjs reports no manifest diff, no migration was added or edited, docs/PRD.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md are untouched, the test manifest gained exactly its six new files at sorted positions, both new strings have message keys, and all fourteen commits name their ticket and carry the Fable trailer. No ticket was claimed 'already satisfied', so no false satisfaction claim exists to disprove. Every new cell that carries a ticket's central claim is non-vacuous against origin/main by construction. Three findings are worth blocking a clean close on. #842's fix is under-scoped against its own stated rationale: the stored basis carries four more cents-typed keys (amount_cents on payroll rows, opening_cents/closing_cents/adjustment_cents on stock rows) that still render as raw sen in the very disclosure the ticket is about, and the lane committed a source comment asserting the opposite while citing the two artifacts that disprove it. #904 wires the new poll's onTick to a whole-bundle reload (5-6 reads per tick) against use-settle-poll.ts's own 'One read' contract and against the README-recorded fix that cut the sibling poll from four reads to one. And apps/web/README.md's Documents section now misdescribes the read #876 changed and says nothing about the poll #904 added, against work-order rule 9 and against the report's explicit claim that no README needed touching. The remaining findings are small: a mis-indented key in the shared en.json, #987's substitution reaching sibling doors untested, #903's grep evidence narrower than its AC and mis-enumerated in the report, and two weak cells (842.absent has no positive anchor, #904's AC3 cell does not exercise a live receipts poll). The lane's own admitted residual stands: no browser walk was run over the four surfaces it touched.
